population.definition: Maseru urban centre, 2016 census (Lesotho Bureau of Statistics figures as compiled by citypopulation.de). The compiler notes the urban centre includes population from Berea district. The only official BoS document read (Preliminary Results Report, Oct 2016) gives the Maseru DISTRICT household population as 516,869 (25.8% of 2,001,946), not the city. Final city table not read; other sites give 330,760 (unverified).

source.title: Lesotho: Districts, Urban Centers & Peri-Urban Centers
source.quote: Maseru includes population from Berea district.

facts.claim: Maseru was proclaimed the capital of the Basotho people in 1869 by Moshoeshoe I, when it was a modest trading outpost.

source.title: Maseru, Lesotho (Research Starter)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Maseru existed as a modest trading outpost when Moshoeshoe I proclaimed it the capital of the Basotho people in 1869.

facts.claim: In the same year colonial forces made Maseru administrative headquarters of the British Basutoland Protectorate. (Note: other sources say it began as a British police camp; accounts differ on who founded it.)

source.title: Maseru, Lesotho (Research Starter)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: colonial forces officially named Maseru the administrative headquarters of the British Basutoland Protectorate

facts.claim: The city began as a police camp before becoming the national capital under British protection.

source.title: Why the name: Maseru?
source.author: Dr. Y.
source.quote: first established as a police camp

facts.claim: The name comes from Sesotho and refers to red sandstone.

source.title: Maseru in Focus
source.author: Lauren Kania
source.quote: a Sesotho word meaning 'red sandstones'

facts.claim: Since then the city has expanded rapidly, with problems such as poverty and overcrowding.

source.title: Maseru, Lesotho (Research Starter)
source.author: Beverly Ballaro
source.quote: Maseru has since expanded rapidly

places.name: Basotho Hat (Mokorotlo) building
places.what: A building in central Maseru designed in the shape of the traditional Basotho conical hat. Described by a tourism site as housing a museum on the nation's history, culture and traditions.

facts.label: Design
facts.value: Building shaped like the traditional hat

source.title: Mokorotlong Maseru Down Town
source.quote: Called the Mokorotlo, the site is a traditional hut redesigned in a more modern and sophisticated style.

facts.label: Use
facts.value: Museum on national history and culture

source.title: Mokorotlong Maseru Down Town
source.quote: The revamped hut houses a museum where visitors can learn more about the nation's history, culture and traditions.

facts.label: Hat origin tradition
facts.value: Hat shape said to be copied from Mount Qiloane next to Thaba Bosiu

source.title: The culture of Basotho: history, people, clothing and food
source.author: Libe Mohale
source.quote: Its shape is said to have been copied from that of Qiloane Mountain which is located next to Thaba Bosiu in Lesotho.

places.name: Thaba Bosiu
places.what: A flat-topped sandstone mountain stronghold about 20 km east of Maseru, used by Moshoeshoe I as residence and fortress. Often called the historic and spiritual heart of the Basotho kingdom. (Not checked whether it is on the UNESCO Tentative List; verify before use.)

facts.label: Distance
facts.value: About 20 km east of Maseru, about 1,800 m

source.title: Thaba Bosiu, Lesotho
source.quote: only 20km East of Maseru

source.title: Thaba Bosiu, Lesotho
source.quote: the chilly midwinter of 1824

source.title: Lesotho- Thaba Bosiu
source.quote: The fortress has eight springs and seven passes, the main one being Khubelu.
